newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal trade deficit widens to $916 mln.
newsitem.headline: Nepal trade deficit widens to $916 mln.

text.p: Nepal's trade deficit widened to 52 billion rupees ($916 million) in the first nine months of fiscal 1996/97, as imports grew faster than exports, Nepal's central bank said on Tuesday.
The deficit stood at 40.3 billion rupees in the same period in 1995/96.

Exports rose 16.3 percent to 17 billion rupees while imports jumped 25.6 percent to 69 billion rupees, when compared with the same nine-month period in 1995/96, the Nepal Rastra Bank said in a statement. Nepal's fiscal year begins in mid-July.
Hand-knotted woollen carpet exports totalled 6.7 billion rupees, while ready-made garment exports were 4.4 billion rupees.

Hand-made carpets, first introduced in the Himalayan kingdom by refugees who fled Tibet with the Dalai Lama in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Chinese rule, and cotton garments are Nepal's two principal exports.

The Nepal Rastra Bank said carpet exports surged 14 percent in the nine months compared to July 1995-April 1996, after growing at 1.7 percent in the previous period, and garment exports rose 16 percent after a decline of 6.5 percent.
Most carpets were sold to Germany, while the United States was the largest buyer of Nepali garments.
Nepal's trade deficit with its giant southern neighbour, India, in the nine months of 1996/97 narrowed slightly to 15.1 billion rupees from 15.9 billion rupees, the bank said.
More than 27 percent of the landlocked kingdom's trade is with India.

Business officials said Nepali exports to India increased after the two countries signed a trade pact last December under which New Delhi allows duty-free imports of all Nepali goods except alcohol, cosmetics and cigarettes.
In return, Nepal gave a 20 percent customs duty discount to Indian imports, making them more competitive than goods sold by other countries in the kingdom.
